name: Bunni
overview: Bunni is a male member of the tribe of Levi, identified specifically as a descendant of Merari. He is noted primarily for being the father of Hashabiah, situating him within the Levitical genealogies. His mention in Nehemiah highlights his role within the post-exilic community's priestly and Levitical structure.
namesAndTitles: The name Bunni appears once in Scripture and does not have a provided meaning or divine origin. It is simply recorded as a proper name in Nehemiah 11:15 without additional explanation.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Bunni as the father of Hashabiah, establishing a direct paternal relationship. Additionally, he is explicitly noted as a descendant of Merari, linking him to one of the main Levitical family lines. Beyond these, no further family relationships are detailed.
scriptureSignificance: Bunni's significance lies in his place within the Levitical lineage, particularly as a descendant of Merari, one of Levi's sons entrusted with specific religious duties. His identification as the father of Hashabiah connects him to the post-exilic restoration community, emphasizing the continuity of Levitical service and heritage. His mention in Nehemiah underscores the importance of genealogical records in maintaining the identity and function of the priestly families after the exile.
